task: What are the details of the VMware acquisition?

c1.note: Broadcom's release confirms closing on Nov 22, 2023; the cash-and-stock and NYSE delisting variants are also supported by the release and the 10-K.

c2.note: Release states VMware common stock will cease to be traded on the NYSE.

c3.note: Announcement dated May 26, 2022 gives a cash-and-stock deal valued at about $61B.

c4.note: Release bases the $61B value on Broadcom's May 25, 2022 closing price.

c5.note: Release says Broadcom will assume $8B of VMware net debt.

c6.note: Both the announcement and the closing 8-K give $142.50 cash or 0.2520 Broadcom shares per VMware share, subject to proration.

c7.note: Release states the election was prorated to about 50% cash and 50% stock; the 8-K confirms 50% each.

c8.note: Release gives total per-share consideration of $138.23 based on the May 25, 2022 Broadcom close.

c9.note: The 44% premium was measured against VMware's May 20, 2022 close, and is stale background.

c10.note: The 10-K reports about $30.8B cash plus 544M shares worth $53.4B at close, so the stock component moved with AVGO's price (deal about $69B incl. debt per Reuters); this is a general inference.

c11.note: The announcement projected 88%/12% ownership, which is stale background.

c13.note: Release states $32B in new fully committed debt financing commitments.

c15.note: The go-shop was 40 days, expiring 11:59 p.m. PT on July 5, 2022; this is stale history.

c16.note: Press release states the agreement was unanimously approved by both boards.

c17.note: Release says Broadcom Software Group will rebrand and operate as VMware after closing.

c18.note: Release states the target of about $8.5B pro forma EBITDA within three years post-closing.

c19.note: $61B valuation was based on the May 25, 2022 price, with $8B net debt assumed in addition.

c20.note: Announcement framing used the May 2022 price; the 10-K total purchase consideration of $86,290M includes stock, cash, term loan retirement and equity awards.

c21.note: CMA describes the deal as $69B: $61B equity plus $8B debt.

c23.note: Cleary says the transaction was valued at approx. $87B at signing; the 'likely including debt' gloss is a reasonable inference but differs from the $69B announcement figure.

c24.note: Reuters and TechTarget report $69B; the figure is widely used.

c25.note: No passage addresses it, but it matches known history: the closing date was extended several times (Broadcom extended the outside date to Nov 2023).

c26.note: Reuters states the EC approved after Broadcom offered remedies to help rival Marvell.

c27.note: CMA cleared the deal after a Phase 2 in-depth investigation.

c29.note: Cleary refers to an 18-month regulatory review process.

c30.note: Cleary lists the US, UK, Canada and Japan among the unconditional clearances.

c31.note: Cleary states the EC, Korea and China conditionally cleared the deal.

c32.note: EC approved on July 12, 2023 conditional on commitments with a 10-year duration, as I know it; the passage is garbled but the press release date matches.

c33.note: EC remedies covered interoperability, API access and technical support, source-code access and separation, protecting Fibre Channel HBA rivals (Marvell, Emulex); consistent with Reuters.

c35.note: 10-K states 544 million shares with fair value of $53,398 million.

c36.note: Total purchase consideration 86,290 million per table.

c37.note: Net of cash acquired $79,648 million per table.

c38.note: Cash acquired is 6,642 million per table.

c39.note: 10-K says it assumed $8,250 million of VMware senior unsecured notes.

c40.note: 10-K says 2.52 shares on a split-adjusted basis; the original ratio was 0.2520 (10-for-1 split).

c41.note: 10-K states EUC sold to KKR July 1, 2024 for $3.5 billion cash after working capital adjustments.

c42.note: Broadcom continues to operate VMware (VCF) after the EUC sale, per the 10-K.

c43.note: Filing is for the fiscal year ended Nov 2, 2025 with holders count as of Nov 28, 2025, so a mid-December filing is consistent; the exact date of December 18, 2025 is not shown but is plausible.

c44.note: Closing release says it will invest in VMware Cloud Foundation, the foundation of private and hybrid clouds.

c45.note: Closing release lists Tanzu, Application Networking (Load Balancing), Advanced Security and Software-Defined Edge.

c46.note: The EU and China conditionally cleared the deal after antitrust review, and the move to subscription licensing is well known, though the passages show scrutiny of the deal itself rather than of the licensing change.

c47.note: Business Insider said cost-cutting has 'at least halved' VMware's workforce, with about 16,000 employees by January 2025; the caveat that this is not a Broadcom disclosure is correct.

c48.note: The TechTarget headline and lede match: after pushing the full private cloud suite, Broadcom is offering a smaller standalone vSphere Express; the pricing caveat was not visible in the excerpt.

c49.note: The search found Bloomberg and Bloomberg Law reports of EU scrutiny of Broadcom's VMware licensing (Feb 2026) and EU information requests to cloud providers (Sept 2026, via PYMNTS). The 'so terms may continue to change' part is an inference, not a reported fact. I could not read the paywalled pages,
